definitions.gloss: to be in charge of; to take charge of
definitions.explanation: To have responsibility for a task, class, area, or group of people.

examples.english: She is in charge of the third-grade class.

examples.english: One teacher is in charge of two classes, so they're very busy.

notes:
{受|う}け{持|も}つ means to have something as one's assigned responsibility — a class, a subject, a district, a set of patients. It describes an ongoing assignment given to you rather than a task you take on by choice, so it is most at home in schools, hospitals, and workplaces where duties are divided up among people. {受|う}け{持|も}っている (the ている form) is the usual way to say what someone is currently in charge of.
